summary: The core is built as a netlist of the Dominos board: the processes and signals are named after chip designators and pins (F2, D2, E8, H8, R2, R3, J9, F9, H9, A7_2, P3_3), the address decode runs through the E2 bipolar PROM and 74LS42/9334-style decoders, and video comes from an H/V counter chain driving a 74LS166 shift register and a 9316 latch. Nothing follows MAME's sprint2_state decomposition. MAME has *_r/*_w handlers, a tilemap and sync_r computed from vpos thresholds; the core builds those same behaviors from raster counter bits and gate logic.

findings.signal: Address decode via bipolar PROM + decoder chips
findings.note: CPU A13-A9 index the E2 PROM, whose outputs feed the one-hot decoders F2, D2 and E8. Gate combinations of those decoder outputs then produce ROM1-4, RAM_n, SYNC_n, SWITCH_n, Timer_Reset_n and H8_en. MAME instead lists address ranges with handler functions.

findings.signal: WRAM aliasing done with address-line OR gates
findings.note: Working RAM at 0x0000 maps onto the top of video RAM because WRAM is ORed into A9-A7. MAME gets the same result in software with m_video_ram[0x380 + offset % 0x80].

findings.signal: Sync/status read from raster signals, not vpos thresholds
findings.note: The read data is VCount(7), VBlank_s, Vreset and Attract, taken straight from the sync register outputs. MAME compares vpos against 261, 224 and 131.

findings.signal: Raster counter chain + sync PROM register
findings.note: The H counter reloads to 0100000000, and the V counter is clocked by the edge of hsync. A sync PROM (M2) is addressed by V bits plus fed-back VBLANK, followed by a register clocked on hsync. Two D flip-flops clocked by H32 and H8 generate HBLANK and HSYNC.

The character ROMs (R4/P4) are addressed by display(5:0)&V4V2V1. Their output loads a shift register (R3) on H1&H2&H4&H256, and R2 latches the color bit and the blanking/sync signals. The pixel color comes from AND gates (A6). MAME instead draws a whole tilemap with a palette.

findings.signal: Video RAM scan address from H/V counter bits
findings.note: Vram_addr is built from V/H bits gated by H256, so the same RAM scan also reaches the motion/sound region during HBLANK. The display bus is latched inverted on phi2 (F5), as on the board.

findings.signal: CPU clock and delayed write from H4 via flip-flop chain
findings.note: phi1 comes from two clk12-registered copies of H4, and WRITE_n goes through a four-stage shift chain (A7). This is the board's own clock and write-strobe derivation, not a generic FPGA clock enable.

findings.signal: Sound latches strobed by H-counter decode of display bus
findings.note: Freq_n and Amp_n decode H-count phases while video hardware scans the RAM and latch Display(3:0). Topple is gated by 4V. MAME takes these as discrete inputs written by the CPU.
The 8-to-1 selectors F9 and H9, the J9 DIP-bank selector with OR and wired-AND logic, and the M8 mux reproduce the board's switch matrix. MAME uses bit shifts such as (val << (offset ^ 7)) & 0x80.
A 4-bit counter clocked by V128 is cleared by the Timer_Reset_n decoder output, and its bit 3 drives the CPU reset.

The analog VCO is approximated with a tuned lookup table and a ramp counter, then divided by a 7492-style counter. These are invented constants, not MAME's resistor-ladder model, so the block points to neither side.
